title: Autopromote: Algorithmic Promotion of Customer Escalations into Roadmap Commitments
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Goal: Reduce time-to-commit for high-value customer escalations by automatically surfacing, scoring, and promoting issues into the product roadmap while preserving human oversight and auditability. We want a predictable, auditable pipeline that converts validated escalations (especially from strategic / high-ARR accounts) into prioritized roadmap candidates when they clear a configurable score threshold.

Scope:
- Design a repeatable scoring model that blends account ARR, renewal proximity, severity (customer-reported impact), feature fit, and signals from support/CS/AE notes.
- Build an autopromotion engine that: (1) ingests validated escalation artifacts, (2) computes a score, (3) when score >= promotion_threshold, auto-creates a PM roadmap ticket with templated fields, (4) notifies relevant squad(s) and exec review if above exec_threshold.
- Provide manual override and audit trail (who promoted/demoted, rationale).
- Integrate with Console dashboards to show queued promotions and historical promotion efficacy (lead-to-commit conversion, time saved).

Non-goals: full replacement of PM prioritization or auto-committing budget; autopromote is a triage-to-roadmap generator, not a guaranteed exec pledge.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Scoring formula defined with weights and data sources documented and reviewed by PM, CS, Sales, and Eng.
2) Autopromotion prototype that ingests sample escalations (Support tickets, CS notes, AE tags) and creates PM tickets in Linear with correct metadata and links.
3) Notification flow to Slack #pm-roadmap and to squad inbox when promotion occurs.
4) Admin UI to adjust promotion_threshold and exec_threshold (Console config or simple admin page).
5) Audit log for every automated action stored in the customer escalation dataset and visible in the ticket thread.
6) Pilot with 5 strategic accounts for 6 weeks with defined success metrics (time-to-roadmap < 72h, false-promotion rate < 15%).

Proposed scoring sketch (example):
- Base score = normalized(ARR) * 0.35 + normalized(renewal_days_to_close inverse) * 0.2 + severity_level * 0.25 + feature_fit_score * 0.15 + manual_escalation_boost * 0.05.
- Exec threshold = 0.85 (requires both score >= threshold and CS director signoff).
- Promotion threshold = 0.65 (auto-create a PM ticket and notify).

Data sources: Support ticket tags (Priority, Severity), CS health score, ARR from SFDC, renewal date, AE qualitative tags, recent Slack escalation threads (keyword match), and NPS comments.

Rollout plan:
1) Design & alignment (2 weeks): finalize formula, thresholds, owners, and pilot accounts.
2) Prototype (3 weeks): lightweight lambda that creates Linear tickets for sample escalations; webhooks for notifications.
3) Pilot (6 weeks): enable autopromote for 5 accounts, monitor metrics and manual override usage.
4) Iterate (4 weeks): adjust weights, hooks to Console admin.
5) Scale & docs (ongoing): add controls for organization-level tuning, provide runbook for customer success and sales.

Metrics for success:
- Median time from escalation validation to roadmap ticket creation (target < 72h).
- % of autopromoted tickets that result in committed work within 90 days (target > 40% for pilot accounts).
- False-promotion rate (pilot target < 15%).
- PM manual undo rate (target < 25% of promotions).

Open questions / risks: 
- Data availability: we need reliable SFDC ARR and renewal data; ENG dependency to add missing fields to the support export (see ENG-2421).
- Signal quality: AE/CS notes are unstructured; may need NLU model to extract intent and feature fit. Budget required for model or rule engine.
- Governance: who can change thresholds? Propose a small steering committee (PM, Head of CS, Sales Ops) for the pilot.
